Note::copy_flat_to¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

template<std::output_iterator<std::string_view> OutIt>
void Note::copy_flat_to(OutIt out) const

Copy Borrowed Cells Into An Output Sequence¶

copy_flat_to() writes every Text or Bytes cell, as a std::string_view, to an output iterator. It is the direct bridge for appending a Note’s flattened cell views to a caller-owned sequence without first allocating the temporary std::vector<std::string_view> returned by vector().

The word copy refers to copying each small view object into the destination; the cell bytes are not copied. A destination such as std::vector<std::string_view> therefore remains borrowed from the source Note. Keep a Note sharing the arena alive while consuming those views.

The output iterator must accept std::string_view directly. To create owning std::string values, use std::transform and construct each string explicitly. This makes the ownership transition visible at the call site rather than hiding potentially large allocations behind copy_flat_to().

Traversal And Cost¶

Cells are emitted once in row-major logical order. Scalar, vector, matrix, and rank-three receivers therefore produce numel() writes; shape is not encoded in the destination. The operation is O(numel()), performs no allocation of its own, and does not decode Text or inspect Bytes. Embedded zero bytes are preserved because each view carries an explicit length.

A defined empty Note performs no writes. An undefined Note and every native Bool, Int64, or Float64 Note are rejected before the first output assignment, so the destination is unchanged on those validation failures. For native dtypes, copy from bools(), integers(), or reals() instead.

Example 1: Append Borrowed Views¶

const auto words = pluss::note::make({"north", "east", "south", "west"});
std::vector<std::string_view> borrowed;
words.copy_flat_to(std::back_inserter(borrowed));

std::cout << '[';
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < borrowed.size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << '"' << borrowed[i] << '"';
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

["north", "east", "south", "west"]

Example 2: Make Ownership Explicit¶

const auto words = pluss::note::make({"north", "east", "south", "west"});
std::vector<std::string> owning;
std::transform(words.begin(), words.end(), std::back_inserter(owning),
               [](std::string_view value) { return std::string(value); });

std::cout << '[';
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < owning.size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << '"' << owning[i] << '"';
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

["north", "east", "south", "west"]

The output looks identical, but the strings now own their bytes and remain valid independently of words.

Example 3: Append Instead Of Replace¶

const auto words = pluss::note::make({"south", "west"}); // keep this alive
std::vector<std::string_view> out{"north", "east"};
words.copy_flat_to(std::back_inserter(out));
for (const auto value : out) std::cout << value << ' ';
std::cout << '\n';

Output¶

north east south west

copy_flat_to() starts at the output iterator supplied by the caller; it does not clear or resize a container itself. Do not replace words above with a temporary expression: the appended views would outlive their arena at the semicolon and become dangling.

Example 4: Bytes Remain Length-Aware¶

const std::array<std::byte, 5> raw{
    std::byte{'A'}, std::byte{0}, std::byte{'B'}, std::byte{0x7f}, std::byte{0xff}};
const auto bytes = pluss::note::bytes(raw);
std::vector<std::string_view> cells;
bytes.copy_flat_to(std::back_inserter(cells));
std::cout << "size=" << cells[0].size() << " hex=";
for (const unsigned char value : cells[0])
  std::cout << std::hex << std::setfill('0') << std::setw(2)
            << static_cast<unsigned int>(value);
std::cout << '\n';

Output¶

size=5 hex=4100427fff

Example 5: Undefined And Typed Notes Reject¶

std::vector<std::string_view> out;
try { pluss::Note::undefined().copy_flat_to(std::back_inserter(out)); }
catch (const pluss::Error&) { std::cout << "undefined copy: rejected\n"; }

const auto ints = pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{3, 1, 4});
try { ints.copy_flat_to(std::back_inserter(out)); }
catch (const pluss::Error&) { std::cout << "Int64 copy: rejected\n"; }

Output¶

undefined copy: rejected
Int64 copy: rejected
